prompts.prompt: We are taking DocIntake to production for a SOC 2 customer next month. Using docs/system-design.md and docs/threat-model.md, design the IAM and resource policies. Write complete policy documents to policies/ingest-role.json, policies/ingest-trust.json, policies/processor-role.json, policies/processor-trust.json, policies/uploads-bucket-policy.json and policies/kms-key-policy.json, and write security-design.md explaining them for our security reviewer. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's integrated mode maps every threat to controls with status and validation method, requires Sids, trust policies, a stated production readiness tier, admin/user separation in key policies, and TLS plus SSE-KMS denies on the bucket. A competent answer gets the role policies roughly right but often gives SecurityAdmin kms:* (breaking T-004), omits the threat mapping or tier, or grants ListBucket.

floor_checks.text: All six policy files parse and every permission-policy statement has a Sid
floor_checks.check: python3 -c "import json,sys;S=(lambda d:d['Statement'] if isinstance(d['Statement'],list) else [d['Statement']]);[json.load(open('policies/%s.json'%f)) for f in ['ingest-trust','processor-trust']];fs=['ingest-role','processor-role','uploads-bucket-policy','kms-key-policy'];sys.exit(0 if all(all(s.get('Sid') for s in S(json.load(open('policies/%s.json'%f)))) for f in fs) else 1)"

floor_checks.text: Ingest role cannot read or list the bucket (T-001)

rubric.criterion: Least privilege matches the access-pattern table
rubric.pass: Ingest: PutObject on incoming/*, PutItem, GenerateDataKey; processor: GetObject incoming/*, PutObject processed/*, UpdateItem only, Decrypt + GenerateDataKey; exact ARNs, no wildcard actions
rubric.partial: One permission broader than the table (for example DeleteObject or whole-bucket resource)
rubric.fail: Wildcard actions or several extra permissions

rubric.criterion: Resource policies close T-002, T-003, T-004
rubric.pass: Bucket denies aws:SecureTransport=false and PutObject without aws:kms; key policy gives SecurityAdmin management actions with no Decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey/ReEncrypt
rubric.partial: Two of the three threats closed
rubric.fail: SecurityAdmin can decrypt, or neither bucket deny present

rubric.criterion: Per-customer isolation is placed where it can work
rubric.pass: Notes that the Lambda role cannot use the end user's cognito sub as an IAM variable, so per-customer prefix isolation (T-001) is enforced by the ingest code choosing incoming/<sub>/ and by the presigned URL's fixed key, with prefix-scoped role resources as defense in depth
rubric.partial: Mentions per-user prefixes but implies IAM alone enforces them

rubric.pass: Threat table for T-001..T-004 with control, mitigation status and validation method; production readiness tier stated (Standard for SOC 2/PII); trust policies for lambda.amazonaws.com; SOC 2 notes; out-of-scope items justified
rubric.partial: Threat mapping present but tier or validation method missing

rubric.criterion: No false defects or invented infrastructure
rubric.pass: Treats 'Resource': '*' in the key policy as 'this key'; does not claim VPCs, WAF or endpoints exist in the design (may recommend them)
rubric.fail: Asserts components the design does not have as existing controls

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Would these policies pass a SOC 2 security review?

prompts.prompt: Partner account 444455556666 needs read-only access to objects under processed/ in docintake-uploads-111122223333 (see docs/system-design.md). The partner's engineers will run a batch job in their account. Write cross-account.md describing every policy needed on our side and on the partner's side, and save each policy as its own JSON file under partner-access/. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate makes cross-account access without condition keys CRITICAL and requires resource-based policies with explicit trust. Because the objects are SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key, the grant also needs a key-policy change; models without the skill often write a bucket policy alone, trust the partner account root with no condition, and forget KMS.

floor_checks.check: ls partner-access/*.json >/dev/null 2>&1 && python3 -c "import json,glob;[json.load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('partner-access/*.json')]"

floor_checks.text: Every Allow statement naming the partner account carries a Condition
floor_checks.check: python3 -c "import json,glob,sys;S=(lambda d:d['Statement'] if isinstance(d['Statement'],list) else [d['Statement']]);hits=[s for f in glob.glob('partner-access/*.json') for s in S(json.load(open(f))) if s.get('Effect')=='Allow' and '444455556666' in json.dumps(s)];sys.exit(0 if hits and all(s.get('Condition') for s in hits) else 1)"

rubric.pass: Bucket (or access point) grant scoped to processed/* plus a key-policy grant of kms:Decrypt to the partner principal, and the partner-side identity policy for their job role
rubric.partial: S3 and partner side covered but KMS missing, or KMS only mentioned in prose
rubric.fail: Only one side of the trust

rubric.pass: Grants a named partner role (or a role in our account they assume with sts:ExternalId); conditions such as aws:PrincipalArn/aws:SecureTransport; kms:ViaService s3 on the decrypt grant; explains confused-deputy if a role trust is used
rubric.partial: Conditions present but principal is the whole partner account root without justification

rubric.pass: Only GetObject (and ListBucket limited by s3:prefix processed/ if listing is needed); no Put/Delete/wildcards
rubric.partial: ListBucket granted without a prefix condition

rubric.pass: Says which party applies which file, how to test (aws s3 cp from the partner role, expected AccessDenied on incoming/), and how to revoke
rubric.partial: Policies clear but no test or revoke path

focus: Would the partner's job actually be able to read SSE-KMS objects?
Clarity of who applies which policy

prompts.prompt: A teammate drafted DocIntake's policies in drafts/ (design and threat model are in docs/). Review them before they go to the security team. Write policy-review.md with findings ordered by severity, each with the file, the statement Sid, why it matters, and the corrected statement. Do not ask questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state your assumptions in your final message.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's gate makes wildcard actions on S3/KMS and cross-account grants without condition keys CRITICAL, and missing aws:SecureTransport IMPORTANT. A reviewer with it also knows that 'Resource': '*' and root delegation in a key policy are normal, and that key admins must not hold use actions. Without it, reviewers either miss the SecurityAdmin kms:* (T-004) and the missing partner KMS grant, or flag the key-policy root statement as a wildcard defect.

floor_checks.text: policy-review.md exists and names the processor s3:* statement

rubric.pass: Flags all three: ProcessorS3 s3:* on the bucket, KeyAdministration giving SecurityAdmin kms:* (T-004), PartnerReadProcessed with no Condition on the partner root

Flags at least three of: no aws:SecureTransport deny (T-002), ingest dynamodb:Scan beyond PutItem, ingest holding kms:Decrypt it does not need, partner lacking kms:Decrypt so the grant cannot work, missing trust policies

rubric.criterion: Severity mapping and ordering follow the skill
rubric.pass: CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION order; wildcard and condition-less cross-account items are CRITICAL; SecureTransport is IMPORTANT; each finding names file and Sid
rubric.partial: Ordered but one gate item placed in the wrong tier
rubric.fail: No severity or no Sid references

rubric.pass: Replacement JSON for each defect is valid and least-privilege (processor Get incoming/* + Put processed/*, admin management-only action list, partner grant with conditions plus KMS)
rubric.partial: Fixes described but JSON missing or partly wrong

rubric.pass: Does not call key-policy 'Resource': '*' or the AccountRoot kms:* statement a defect; does not flag ingest PutObject incoming/* or processor UpdateItem
rubric.partial: One false positive, or flags AccountRoot but with the right caveat
